newsitem.title: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES: SOCCER-KUWAIT KNOCK OUT ASIAN CUP HOLDERS JAPAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KUWAIT KNOCK OUT ASIAN CUP HOLDERS JAPAN.

text.p: Kuwait knocked defending champions Japan out of the Asian Cup with a 2-0 quarter-final win on Sunday.
Striker Jassem Al-Houwaidi scored in each half to put the Japanese out and earn his side a semifinal against hosts the UAE. They beat Iraq 1-0 earlier on Sunday.
An inspired Kuwait, who recorded the tournament's first major upset by beating South Korea 2-0 in the previous round, began the match brightly.

They had the first chance in the fourth minute when a long-range drive from Houwaidi was parried away by keeper Kenichi Shimokawa, although his opposite number Falah Al-Majidi soon had to react quickly to deny Japan's striker Kazuyoshi Miura.

The Kuwaitis broke the deadlock in the 17th minute. Abdullah Seehan pounced on a poor back header by Japanese defender Naoki Soma, before cutting it back from the byline to Houwaidi who fired home from close range.
Japan had a lucky escape in the 53rd minute when the referee produced only the yellow card to Hiroshige Yanagimoto following a professional foul on Abdulaziz.
But the protests instantly turned to celebrations when Houwaidi chased a harmless-looking ball, the goalkeeper made a mess of it and the striker sneaked between two defenders to score.
It was his fifth goal in the Asian Cup, making him the top scorer.
The Japanese then laid siege to the Kuwaiti penalty area but some athletic goalkeeping and brilliant defending kept them at bay.

Japan: 19-Kenichi Shimokawa; 2-Hiroshige Yanagimoto (18- Syojo Jo 80); 3-Naoki Soma; 4-Masami Ihara; 5-Norio Omura; 6- Motohiro Yamaguchi; 7-Yasuto Honda (14-Masayuki Okano 66); 8- Masakiyo Maezono; 9-Takuya Takagi; 10-Hiroshi Nanami; 11- Kazuyoshi Miura.

Kuwait: 21-Falah Al-Majidi; 2-Osama Abdullah; 3-Jamal Abdulrahman; 4-Yousif Al-Dakhi; 5-Mohammad; 7-Bader Al-Halabeej (19-Hani Saqer 69) ; 9-Bashar Abdulaziz; 11-Abdullah Seehan (16- Sami Al-Lenqawi 83); 12-Fawaz Al-Ahmed; 17-Esam Sakeen; 20- Jassem Al-Houwaidi (10-Khaled Fairouz 89).
